Charts of CMSY++ Results

Source: R/cmsy_plot.R
cmsy_plot.Rd

This function draws the results of cmsy_run(). For each stock it draws the charts of the CMSY++ user guide (Froese et al. 2021), from the results saved by the run:

analysis

the six panels A-F of the CMSY++ analysis chart in one figure: catch, the explored and the viable r-k pairs, B/k, F/Fmsy and the equilibrium curve (user guide Figure 1; needs the patchwork package);

catch

catch with the MSY estimate and its 95% confidence band (user guide Figure 1A, 2 upper left);

rk

the posterior r-k pairs (log scales), the prior ranges of r and k (dotted box) and the most likely pair with its 95% limits (Figure 1B, C);

biomass

relative biomass B/k with its 95% band, the B/k prior ranges of the first, intermediate and last years (dashed if from the neural network, solid if given by the user), Bmsy (B/k = 0.5) and half of Bmsy (B/k = 0.25, reduced recruitment) (Figure 1D);

b_bmsy

relative stock size B/Bmsy with its 95% band and lines at Bmsy, 0.8 Bmsy (FAO limit of overfished) and 0.5 Bmsy (Figure 2 upper right);

exploitation

F/Fmsy with its 95% band and Fmsy (Figure 1E, 2 lower left);

equilibrium

the Schaefer equilibrium curve of catch/MSY against B/k, indented below B/k = 0.25, with the predicted path from the first (square) to the last year (triangle) (Figure 1F);

management

the four management panels in one figure: catch with MSY, B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy and the Kobe plot (Figure 2; without the patchwork package, the first three panels);

kobe

Kobe plot: the path of B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy from the first (square) through the intermediate (circle) to the last year (triangle), the last-year posterior draws with the 50, 80 and 95% probability regions, and the probability of each quadrant (Figure 3);

prior_posterior

prior and posterior densities of r, k, MSY and B/k in the first, intermediate and last years, with the prior-posterior variance ratio PPVR (Figure 4);

retrospective

B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy when the last one, two or three years are left out, with Mohn's rho (Figure 5; needs cmsy_run(plots = "retrospective"));

mcmc

the draws of each MCMC chain (trace) and their densities for r, k, MSY and the last-year B/k, with Rhat and the effective sample size (see cmsy_mcmc(); not for runs of earlier versions of the package).

For several stocks together:

overview

last-year B/Bmsy of each stock with its 95% limits, coloured by status;

kobe_all

last-year B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy of all stocks in a Kobe plot, sized by catch;

status

share of stocks and of last-year catch in each status class;

status_time

the same shares in every year, by number of stocks and weighted by catch;

histogram

distribution of the last-year B/Bmsy, with the class limits;

b_bmsy_all

B/Bmsy of every stock over time (small multiples);

trend

median B/Bmsy of the stocks by year (with the interquartile range) and the share of stocks below 0.8 Bmsy;

aggregate

total catch relative to total MSY, and total biomass relative to total Bmsy, of the stocks with results in each year;

map

median last-year B/Bmsy of the stocks of each FAO fishing area on a map.

Status classes (classes) follow FAO (2026) for catch-only (Tier 3) results by default: maximally sustainably fished (B/Bmsy at least 0.8) or overfished. classes = "palomares" uses the five classes of Palomares et al. (2018), used by many CMSY studies: healthy (at least 1), slightly overfished (0.8-1), overfished (0.5-0.8), grossly overfished (0.2-0.5) and collapsed (below 0.2).

Usage

cmsy_plot(
  result,
  stocks = NULL,
  charts = c(cmsy_stock_charts, cmsy_summary_charts),
  classes = c("fao", "palomares"),
  annotations = getOption("faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations", FALSE),
  lang = NULL,
  pptx = getOption("faofishingreport.pptx", FALSE),
  plot_show = fao_setting("plot_show"),
  silent = fao_setting("silent"),
  mcmc_colors = NULL
)

Arguments

result

The result of cmsy_run().

stocks

Optional stocks to draw: Stock identifiers or species, by English or Chinese FAO name, scientific name or FAO 3-alpha code. Default is NULL, all stocks that ran.

charts

The charts to draw (listed in the description above). Default is all of them.

classes

The status classes: "fao" (default, two classes) or "palomares" (five classes).

annotations

The text added to the axis titles and labels: FALSE (default) none, TRUE all, or any of "title", "subtitle", "caption", "legend" and "labels" (text inside the chart). The default can be changed for the session with options(faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations = TRUE).

lang

The language of the chart text and names: "en" (English), "zh" (Chinese) or "both" (Chinese and English). Default is NULL, which uses the language set with fao_settings() ("en" unless changed).

pptx

A logical value. If TRUE, the charts are also saved as editable PowerPoint files in figures/pptx/cmsy/<stock>/ and figures/pptx/cmsy/summary/. Default is FALSE, which can be changed for all functions with fao_settings(pptx = TRUE).

plot_show

A logical value. If TRUE, each chart is also drawn in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved, to look at it at once. Default is FALSE, which can be changed for all functions with fao_settings(plot_show = TRUE). The charts are saved as files (plot = TRUE) either way.

silent

A logical value. If FALSE (default), a progress bar shows how many stocks have been drawn. If TRUE, nothing is printed. The default can be changed for the session with fao_settings(silent = TRUE).

mcmc_colors

Colours of the chains in the "mcmc" chart: NULL (default) for the Okabe-Ito colours, a palette name or a vector of colours (see cmsy_mcmc()).

Value

Invisibly, a named list of the ggplot objects.

Details

By default the charts show only the axis titles and axis labels, so they can be used directly in reports with captions of their own. Titles, subtitles, captions (method, data and prior sources), legends and text inside the charts (probabilities, PPVR, Mohn's rho) are added with annotations.

Charts are saved in figures/png/cmsy/<stock>/ and figures/png/cmsy/summary/ (and as PowerPoint when pptx is TRUE). CMSY++'s own JPEG charts are in the folder of each stock (see result$summary$folder).

References

Froese, R., Demirel, N., Coro, G. and Winker, H. (2021). User Guide for CMSY++. GEOMAR, Germany, 17 pp. https://oceanrep.geomar.de/id/eprint/52147/

Palomares, M.L.D., Froese, R., Derrick, B., Noel, S.-L., Tsui, G., Woroniak, J. and Pauly, D. (2018). A preliminary global assessment of the status of exploited marine fish and invertebrate populations. A report prepared by the Sea Around Us for OCEANA. University of British Columbia and GEOMAR. https://www.fishbase.de/rfroese/OceanaFinalReport_V7a.pdf

FAO (2026). The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026. Rome, FAO. Section "The status of fishery resources", Box 1.3 (assessment tiers and status classes). https://openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/09d03e2f-7097-4d59-bf94-db65e95f44fd/content/sofia-2026/the-status-fishery-resources.html

Mohn, R. (1999). The retrospective problem in sequential population analysis: an investigation using cod fishery and simulated data. ICES Journal of Marine Science 56: 473-488. doi:10.1006/jmsc.1999.0481

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# result <- cmsy_run(...), see cmsy_run()

# All charts in Chinese, with axis text only (the default)
cmsy_plot(result, lang = "zh")

# Kobe plot and prior-posterior densities of one species, with all annotations
cmsy_plot(result, stocks = "Mallotus villosus", charts = c("kobe", "prior_posterior"),
          annotations = TRUE, lang = "both")

# Only titles and legends
cmsy_plot(result, annotations = c("title", "legend"))

# Status of all stocks in the five classes of Palomares et al. (2018), with legends
cmsy_plot(result, charts = c("status", "status_time", "histogram", "map"), classes = "palomares",
          annotations = "legend")

# The management chart also as editable PowerPoint
cmsy_plot(result, charts = "management", pptx = TRUE)

# Annotations for the rest of the session
options(faofishingreport.cmsy_annotations = TRUE)
} # }
